title: Cyclotomic norm-defect threshold (2r)^{phi(n)}=p is the EXACT crossover for N0, E_r, AND T_h
evidence: Two exact integer probes at proper-subgroup dyadic primes (n in {8,16,32}, q~n^4, mu_n a proper subgroup), scripts/probes/_407_conn/C065_threshold_coincidence.py and C065_tangent_norindex.py. (1) The 'EXACT crossover' for E_r vs the norm threshold is FALSE: defect onset r_E is consistently STRICTLY above the norm-threshold onset r_N. n=8,p=4129/4153: r_N=5 but E_r=E_r^(0) clean through r=6 (r_E unobserved, gap>=2). n=16,p=65537: r_N=3, r_E=4. n=16,p=65521: r_N=2, no defect through r=5. n=32,p=1048609: r_N=2, r_E=4 (gap=2); p=1048897: r_N=2, no defect through r=4. So (2r)^{phi(n)}>=p is only the PROVEN one-sided NECESSARY condition (the in-tree no_spurious_tuple_of_lt_prime), NOT a crossover -- the converse (threshold crossed => defect) is exhibited false. Defect onset is governed by actual short +-1 root-of-unity relations mod p (the Bourgain-Shkredov wall), strictly looser than the norm box. (2) The third leg (T_h) is conceptually ill-typed: the tangent sum T_h = sum_{w in mu_n} phi(1-w) is a SINGLE scalar per character phi with NO r-index, so 'T_h crosses at (2r)^{phi(n)}=p' is not well-defined. Worse, T_h has no char-0 value to 'leave': via the proven identity I4 (tangentSum_mul_orderOf_eq_sum_jacobiSum), T = (1/m) sum_i J(chi^i,phi), and Jacobi sums satisfy |J|=sqrt(p) EXACTLY (Weil) at every prime with no clean range -- verified |J(chi^a,chi^b)|=sqrt(521)=22.8254 for all tested (a,b). The probe further shows max_phi|T_h| = n-1 EXACTLY (n=8->7, 16->15, 32->31), attained at the PRINCIPAL character (n-1 unit terms), a trivial combinatorial max, not a defect from an archimedean Jacobi value.
honest_note:
The PROVEN content of CyclotomicNormDefectThreshold.lean (no_spurious_tuple_of_lt_prime: (2r)^{phi(n)}

E_r=E_r^(0)) is correct and stands -- the refutation is of the C065 CONNECTION's stronger 'EXACT crossover, unified across THREE objects' claim, not of any in-tree theorem. The file itself already honestly states the threshold is NECESSARY/vacuous in the prize regime (phi(n)=n/2, p^{1/phi(n)}->1), consistent with leg-1 here. Legs N0 and E_r are the same object (E_r is the spurious-tuple count), so 'three objects' is really two. The genuinely independent third leg (T_h) is the one that fails to type-check against an r-threshold and lacks any char-0 reference value. Numerics are at q~n^4 (n<=32); the conceptual points (no r-index, |J|=sqrt(p) always, max|T|=n-1 at principal char) are q-regime-independent. This refutation belongs in DISPROOF_LOG: the unification 'same threshold (2r)^{phi(n)}=p for N0, E_r, and T_h' does not hold -- E_r's defect onset overshoots the norm threshold, and T_h has neither an r-index nor a char-0 value to make the crossover statement meaningful.
